question: A normal serum PSA level reliably excludes the diagnosis of prostate cancer in a man with lower urinary tract symptoms.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Correct — false. PSA is not a reliable screening test in isolation; prostate cancer can exist with a normal PSA, especially early or well-differentiated disease. PSA must be interpreted alongside DRE findings and clinical context.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: This is false. PSA is prostate-specific, not cancer-specific; it can be normal in early localised prostate cancer. A raised PSA is also not diagnostic of cancer, as BPH and prostatitis also elevate PSA. Clinical judgement and biopsy are required.
